Although the clinical interpretation (positive/negative) is pending, in most validated PCR assays (e.g., BD Max, Xpert C. diff, AmpliVue), a cycle threshold (Ct) value of ~10 corresponds to *very high bacterial load*, far below the typical positivity cutoff (often Ct < 35–40 depending on assay), and is virtually always associated with true toxin gene presence and clinically relevant CDI. Such a low Ct strongly suggests robust amplification of the *tcdB* (and/or *tcdA*) gene — indicating toxigenic *C. difficile* colonization and high likelihood of active infection. Given the classic risk factor (recent fluoroquinolone), symptom profile (profuse watery diarrhea without systemic inflammation), and highly positive molecular signal, CDI is the dominant, unifying diagnosis — even before formal report adjudication. Alternative diagnoses (e.g., viral gastroenteritis, osmotic diarrhea, endocrine causes like hyperthyroidism or VIPoma) are far less likely given the temporal antibiotic exposure and magnitude of diarrheal burden.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Clostridioides difficile infection
